correctness.rationale: The proof reduces the problem to X=s^{T_0} on the discrete lattice {s,s^2,...}. The function phi(x)=x log(x)/log(s) is strictly concave and equals t s^t at lattice point s^t. Its polygonal interpolant through consecutive lattice points is concave, so Jensen gives the sharp upper tilted moment M_+. The lower inequality M>=p is pointwise and its nonattainment for p<s is explicit. The {1,N} construction approaches M=p, mixtures fill all intermediate M, and the published variance formula is affine decreasing in M. Boundary p=s forces T_0=1. No finite experiment is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: At fixed q and p the mean completion time is already fixed, so the theorem answers the natural next question: exactly how much variance can remain hidden behind identical mean-determining success data. The result is a complete sharp finite-p classification with natural extremizers, strengthens the motivating paper's continuous Jensen control by using the integer lattice, and can be used to calibrate finite-p uncertainty in exponential approximations. The slice is not arbitrary: p is the central sufficient statistic of the memoryless-catastrophe model.
